Mechanism our reader should keep: a stablecoin is a bearer claim on dollars held in US Treasuries, so every corridor Circle opens converts a merchant, a freelancer or a remittance recipient in Karachi, Lagos, Manila or Cairo into a holder of US government debt, and the interest on those reserves accrues to the issuer, not the holder. That is the business model stated honestly — Circle earns the float on other people's savings. Then the sovereignty question, which is the one that matters and is rarely put plainly: digital dollarisation is genuinely useful to a worker whose currency loses a third of its value a year, and it simultaneously removes that worker from the domestic monetary system, weakens the central bank's transmission, and shifts seigniorage to Washington — both things are true and the piece must hold both. Report what regulators have actually done: Nigeria's, Pakistan's, Egypt's and Indonesia's positions on stablecoins, the licensing regimes Tazapay holds, and what remittance costs are today against the World Bank's global average. Compare the fee honestly, since the case for this is real. CoinDesk is single-source and reader-aligned; verify the deal terms and Tazapay's licences independently.

stories.label: We must pace the frontier
stories.summary: Dario Amodei's own essay arguing the AI frontier should be paced — 718 points and 976 comments on Hacker News, and the primary document behind two days of reaction coverage we have already run. Write the text, not the reaction: our 09-12 piece covered the call itself and our 09-13 piece covered Angela Rayner's response, so this one must be the close reading neither could be. THIRD AND FINAL entry in this arc. Lead with what the document concretely proposes and what it conspicuously does not: quote the actual mechanisms it names — evaluation thresholds, deployment gates, compute reporting, whatever is there — and separate them into things a single lab can do unilaterally, things that require an agreement between a handful of labs, and things that require a state with subpoena power. That taxonomy is the whole analysis, because pacing is only meaningful at the third level and the essay is written from the first. Mechanism our reader should keep: an actor calling for a slowdown while holding a frontier position is making an argument whose credibility rests entirely on whether it is enforceable against a defector — so name who the addressees are, what happens if one of them declines, and what the essay says about labs outside US jurisdiction, which is the question that decides whether any of it binds. Report the strongest counter-argument fairly: that unilateral restraint transfers the frontier rather than slowing it. Then the part written from nowhere else and the reason this belongs in our feed: pacing is a governance proposal authored by the parties being governed, and the states that would bear the consequences of getting it wrong — Indonesia, Nigeria, Egypt, Pakistan, the Gulf — are neither signatories nor consulted, which is the same structure as the BRICS AI question we wrote on 09-13 arriving from the opposite direction. Do not re-argue that piece. SOURCING: treat the essay as a primary document, quote it, and do not present its framing as consensus.

stories.label: Luminescence dating pushes age of South Dakota's Mammoth Site back by more than 100,000 years
stories.summary: Dozens of mammoths died in a South Dakota sinkhole long thought to be about 26,000 years old; luminescence dating published in Quaternary Research now puts the deposit at more than 160,000 years. Lead with the size of the revision and then immediately with why it was possible at all, because the method is the story: radiocarbon has a hard ceiling near 50,000 years — beyond about ten half-lives there is too little carbon-14 left to measure — so every site older than that was, until recently, dated by inference from stratigraphy rather than measured. Explain optically stimulated luminescence plainly and it is genuinely elegant: buried quartz and feldspar grains accumulate trapped electrons from ambient radiation at a roughly steady rate, and light releases them, so the glow when a grain is stimulated in a lab counts how long since sunlight last reached it — the method dates the burial of the sediment, not the animal, and the piece must say so, because that distinction is where the argument will be. Report the actual measurements: how many samples, from which units, the equivalent dose and environmental dose rate, the error bars, and what the previous radiocarbon or stratigraphic basis for 26,000 years was. Then be honest about the consequence, which is real but bounded: a mammoth trap from a different interglacial is a different ecosystem, a different climate and a different species mix, so the reinterpretation changes what the site is evidence of — and if any human-association claim rested on the old date, say what happens to it. Avoid 'rewrites history' register; a measurement replaced an inference, and that sentence is the lesson. Name the institutions, the authors and the journal.

stories.label: Optimization of Sn-alloyed BaZrS3 chalcogenide perovskite solar cells via charge transport layer engineering
stories.summary: Researchers report device modelling and charge-transport-layer engineering for tin-alloyed BaZrS3, a chalcogenide perovskite solar absorber, aimed at closing the gap between its theoretical promise and its measured efficiency. Lead with what makes this material class worth reporting at all, and state it as a trade the reader can evaluate: the halide perovskites that have dominated solar research for a decade reach very high efficiencies and contain lead and decompose in humidity, while chalcogenide perovskites like BaZrS3 are made of barium, zirconium and sulfur, are chemically stable in air and water, and are nowhere near the efficiency — so the field is trading a decade of performance for durability and non-toxicity, and whether that trade pays is an open question this paper addresses rather than settles. Mechanism our reader will follow: a solar cell is not only its absorber — the electron and hole transport layers on either side must have band edges that line up with the absorber's, or carriers recombine at the interface before they reach a contact, and 'transport layer engineering' means searching that alignment. Say what tin alloying does to the bandgap and why that matters against the Shockley-Queisser optimum. Report the specifics precisely and label them honestly: which layers were tested, what efficiency was obtained, and — critically — whether this is simulation (SCAPS-1D or similar) or fabricated devices, because the difference is enormous and modelling papers are routinely reported as breakthroughs. State the limitations the authors themselves give. Then the structural why: lead-free, humidity-stable, earth-abundant photovoltaics matter most where panels sit in heat and monsoon humidity without a recycling regime behind them — Pakistan, Indonesia, Nigeria, the Gulf — and toxicity is a disposal question those markets will meet first. Accepted manuscript with a permanent DOI, not the version of record; say so.
